brief: Yesterday's post-Fed move left the S&P closing less than 1.1% below Goldman's short-term CTA sell threshold, putting systematic selling risk back in focus. Today's roughly 1.1% SPX rally reversed that: Goldman says the CTA selling threat now looks considerably smaller and expects the rally to moderate the flows implied by yesterday's scenario estimates ($5.4bn of SPX selling in a flat tape, $54bn in a down tape, versus $17bn of buying in an up tape). Coming into today, CTAs were estimated long only $37.5bn of US equities, the 22nd percentile on a one-year lookback. Fundamental hedge funds are also far from maxed out: Goldman Prime puts US L/S gross leverage at the 31st percentile and net leverage at the 5th percentile over the past year. Sentiment is washed out too, with the AAII Bull-Bear spread at new 2026 lows and near post-ChatGPT-era depths, though Goldman still expects it needs more time before meaningful re-risking. Hedge funds also aggressively dumped macro products last week, the largest net selling Goldman has recorded since Liberation Day.
